**No—not as a current assessment.** The June 2025 file was based on observations through 2024. A newer analysis, run on 12 November 2026, detected **13.5 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2025**, or 3.91% of the property.

The JRC reference classified 98% of the affected area as forest in 2020. However, the event does not yet meet the tool’s corroboration rule because the series has not observed a later year. The annual data also do not establish whether the loss occurred before or after the June 2025 assessment.

The latest observations extend through 2025, so they do not address possible loss in 2026. The due-diligence file should be updated and the event investigated.
